//: Directory-local tsconfig for #31. It exists because #24's review flagged that
claiming a shared-config change is unavoidable requires first evaluating a
local one -- and a local one does work.
Two load-bearing details, both found by measuring rather than assuming:
1. `react` must map to @types/react, NOT to the runtime package (which ships
no declarations). Mapping the runtime package makes every importer --
legacy sources included -- lose its types. This is the mistake #24 made
2. There must be NO `"*"` catch-all in `paths`. A catch-all shadows normal
node resolution for the legacy sources this program pulls in, and they
then fail to find their own @types. `packages/react-ui` typechecks with 0
errors under its own config, so any error in those files is this config's
fault, not a legacy defect. Only the specifiers OUR files import are
mapped; legacy sources resolve their own dependencies by normal walk-up
